newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Petron dips 6.45 pct on peso concerns.
newsitem.headline: Petron dips 6.45 pct on peso concerns.

text.p: Philippine oil refiner Petron Corp shed 40 centavos, or 6.45 percent, to 5.80 pesos in late Wednesday trade on fears the peso may be devalued, brokers said.
"Petron is likely to be a loser when the peso depreciates and its first half earnings are not likely to be spectacular," said Noel Reyes, vice-president at Anscor-Hagedorn Securities.
Traders said Petron is one issue which will be negatively affected by a weakening of the peso due to its crude and petroleum product imports.
Talk of the peso being devalued surfaced on Wednesday after the Singapore Straits Times said it was to be discussed at a meeting of the Philippine Monetary Board on Wednesday.
The newspaper attributed the information to Trade Secretary Cesar Bautista but he denied it.
